items.stem: Which of the following statements about indentured servitude is true?
options: (A) Indentured servitude was the means by which most Africans came to the New World.
(B) Indentured servitude never attracted many people because its terms were too harsh.
(C) Approximately half of all indentured servants died before earning their freedom.
(D) Indenture was one of several systems used to distinguish house enslaved people from field enslaved people.
items.explanation: Indentured servitude promised freedom and a parcel of land to those who survived its seven-year term of service. However, fewer than half of indentured servants succeeded. Most worked in the fields performing grueling labor, and many died as a result. Indentured servitude was overwhelmingly a system for English immigrants, and nearly 100,000 took advantage of it.

option_explanations.A: Most Africans arrived in the New World through the transatlantic slave trade as enslaved laborers, not as indentured servants. Indentured servitude was overwhelmingly a system for European immigrants, above all the English.
option_explanations.B: Indentured servitude did attract large numbers — roughly 100,000 English immigrants took indentures in the 17th century alone. The terms were harsh, but poverty in England made the bargain attractive to many.
option_explanations.C: Mortality among indentured servants was extremely high, especially in the Chesapeake, where disease and grueling field labor killed roughly half before their seven-year terms ended. Fewer than half survived to claim freedom and land.
option_explanations.D: Indentured servitude and slavery were distinct legal systems, not categories for sorting enslaved people. Indenture applied mainly to European immigrants working off the cost of passage, while enslaved Africans were held in lifelong bondage.

items.stem: The philosophy of mercantilism holds that economic power resides primarily in
options: (A) surplus labor power and control over raw materials
(B) control of hard currency and a positive trade balance
(C) the ability to extend and receive credit at favorable interest rates
(D) domination of the slave trade and control of the shipping lanes
items.explanation: During the Colonial Era, the British subscribed to the economic theory of mercantilism, which held that a favorable balance of trade and control of hard currency were the keys to economic power. Ultimately, the theory of capitalism, famously championed by Adam Smith, supplanted mercantilism as the predominant economic theory of the West.

option_explanations.A: Surplus labor as a measure of economic power belongs to later theories of value, not to mercantilism. Mercantilists did not define national wealth in terms of labor power.
option_explanations.B: Mercantilism measured a nation's economic power by its stock of hard currency (gold and silver) and pursued a favorable balance of trade — exporting more than importing — so that specie flowed into the country.
option_explanations.C: Credit and interest rates are concerns of financial capitalism, not of mercantilist doctrine, which centered on bullion and the balance of trade.
option_explanations.D: Commanding the slave trade and shipping lanes could serve a mercantilist empire, but they are not what the philosophy defines economic power as. The definition is about hard currency and a positive trade balance.

items.stem: Which of the following colonies was NOT founded for reasons grounded in religious conflict?
options: (A) Pennsylvania
(B) Rhode Island
(C) Massachusetts
(D) Georgia
items.explanation: Many of the northern colonies were founded in the 17th century by those seeking a haven from religious strife or persecution. In contrast, Georgia was founded in 1732 as a refuge for indebted prisoners and also as a buffer colony to protect the southern colonies from potential Spanish invasion.

option_explanations.A: Pennsylvania was founded by William Penn (1681) as a refuge for Quakers, who faced persecution in England — a founding grounded in religious conflict.
option_explanations.B: Rhode Island was founded by Roger Williams (1636) after Massachusetts banished him for religious dissent — a founding grounded in religious conflict.
option_explanations.C: Massachusetts Bay was founded by Puritans (1630) seeking to build a reformed godly community — a founding grounded in religious conflict.
option_explanations.D: Georgia (1732) was founded by James Oglethorpe as a refuge for indebted prisoners and as a military buffer protecting the southern colonies from Spanish Florida — social and strategic reasons, not religious conflict.

items.stem: Which of the following is the best explanation for why the British did not establish a powerful central government in the American colonies?
options: (A) The British cared little how the colonists lived so long as the colonies remained a productive economic asset.
(B) Britain feared that the colonists would rebel against any substantial government force that it established.
(C) Few members of the British elite were willing to travel to the colonies, even for the opportunity to govern.
(D) Britain gave the colonies a large measure of autonomy as a first step in transitioning the region to independence.
items.explanation: Provided the colonies continued to buy British goods and to supply the British with raw materials, England did not care how the colonies governed themselves. England did impose its will (through the vice-admiralty courts) when the colonies attempted to shirk their economic responsibilities but otherwise took a laissez-faire approach. As a result, the colonies developed a tradition of independence that contributed to their eventual rebellion against the Crown.

option_explanations.A: Britain's interest in the colonies was economic: raw materials in, manufactured goods out. As long as trade flowed, London was content to leave colonial self-government alone — the policy later called salutary neglect.
option_explanations.B: Britain was not holding back out of fear of rebellion. In the 17th and early 18th centuries it simply did not care to govern closely; when it finally did assert authority in the 1760s, rebellion followed.
option_explanations.C: British officials did serve in the colonies — royal governors, customs collectors, admiralty judges. Unwillingness to travel was not the reason for weak central government.
option_explanations.D: Britain never planned to hand the colonies independence. The autonomy they enjoyed was neglect, not a deliberate transition.

items.stem: Which of the following statements best defines the early interactions between English colonists and Native Americans in the New World?
options: (A) English colonists viewed Native Americans as a potential workforce and largely aimed to enslave them in the regions they colonized.
(B) English colonists largely avoided contact or relations with Native Americans as much as possible in the regions they colonized.
(C) English colonists maintained friendly relations with Native Americans and sought alliances with them in the regions they colonized.
(D) English colonists considered Native Americans as valuable trading partners and depended on their skills and knowledge with the land to their mutual benefit in the regions they colonized.
items.explanation: Unlike most other early European colonizing powers, English settlers aimed to avoid contact and relations with Native Americans. Choices (A), (C), and (D) describe the early interactions between Native Americans and the Spanish, French, and Dutch, respectively.

option_explanations.A: Trying to enslave Native Americans as a workforce was the Spanish approach under the encomienda, not the English one. English attempts to enslave Native people were limited and largely failed.
option_explanations.B: Unlike the Spanish, French, and Dutch, English colonists generally sought to avoid sustained contact with Native Americans, displacing them rather than incorporating them as laborers, allies, or trading partners.
option_explanations.C: Friendly alliances were the French pattern — for example, the French alliance with the Huron in the fur trade — not the English one.
option_explanations.D: Depending on Native trading partners describes the Dutch (and partly the French) in the fur trade. The English relied far less on Native trade and knowledge of the land.
